assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP turned the CMB anisotropy spectrum into precision measurements of age, geometry, matter content and dark energy, and gave the standard cosmological model its parameters. This is a discovery driven by clues from nature, with lasting impact on every cosmology question, including the dark-energy questions I care about.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a central instrument and observing-strategy figure, and Spergel led the cosmological interpretation. The three-name configuration is plausible, though other WMAP team leaders (e.g. Wilkinson, deceased) and the COBE and Planck precedents complicate the story; I rely on memory here and have not verified the details.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: results confirmed independently and extended by Planck, ACT and SPT over two decades. Recognition is not premature, and arguably overdue given the 2006 and 2019 prizes nearby.
uncertainties: How the committee weighs WMAP against the COBE prize (2006) and Peebles's 2019 prize so it does not look like repeating recognition.
Whether the Nobel statutes allow adequately excluding the broader collaboration and Planck leadership.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, and the evidence tying one to the blazar TXS 0506+056, opened neutrino astronomy through a kilometre-scale detector built in Antarctic ice. This is a real new window on the universe and a clear discovery.
assessment.attribution: Only one credited name is supplied, so a solo award is the only option from this entry. Halzen is the scientific driver and spokesperson of IceCube, but a discovery of this scale rests on a very large collaboration, and I cannot verify how the committee would divide credit with others such as AMANDA pioneers who are not listed here.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux well established since 2013 and the Galactic-plane and NGC 1068 results in 2022-2023 add independent support; source identification is still evolving, but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Single-name credit may under-represent essential contributors to a collaboration-scale discovery.
Source identification of the neutrino flux is still incomplete, which could make a citation to 'discovery' vs 'astronomy' contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of X-ray, optical and radio afterglows of gamma-ray bursts in 1997 settled the long-standing question of their distance and cosmological origin, and with it a class of the most energetic explosions known. A textbook discovery that changed a field overnight.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX discovery of X-ray afterglow and rapid localisation; Kulkarni led the optical, redshift and radio follow-up showing cosmological distance. The decisive observers appear represented, but others (e.g. van Paradijs, deceased; Metzger and Djorgovski for redshift work) complicate a clean three-person split, and I cannot verify this independently.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with nearly three decades of consistent confirmation, and later links to supernovae and neutron-star mergers. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the BeppoSAX team and the ground-based optical groups, plus the deceased contributors.
Whether the committee views this as astronomy rather than physics proper.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 observation of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and was possible only because of two enormous detectors designed and built over two decades. The theory part was recognised in 2013; recognising the experimental achievement is a natural completion and a discovery of enormous significance.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee were founding conceivers, spokespersons and leaders of CMS and ATLAS, which gives a symmetric two-experiment configuration. However, the actual observation involved thousands of physicists and the discovery analyses were led by many others; attribution to founders versus analysts is the central difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and confirmed by two independent experiments, with coupling measurements maturing for over a decade.
uncertainties: Whether the committee is comfortable honouring detector leadership rather than the discovery analysis leaders.
Collaboration-scale credit raises the statutes' three-person limit as a serious practical obstacle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2005 detection of the baryon acoustic peak in galaxy clustering by SDSS and 2dFGRS turned a feature predicted from early-universe physics into a standard ruler, giving an independent route to the expansion history and dark energy. It connects directly to the physics of the early universe and is a clean observational clue about dark energy.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein (SDSS LRG detection) and Cole/Percival (2dFGRS detection and analysis) are the leading names for the two independent 2005 detections; the pairing is reasonable though other 2dFGRS and SDSS leaders could be argued, and I have not verified who is most decisive.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by BOSS, eBOSS and DESI, and now a core part of the cosmological toolkit. Recent DESI hints of evolving dark energy add interest but do not weaken the basic discovery.
uncertainties: Whether this is judged as a measurement technique rather than a fundamental discovery, relative to the WMAP candidate.
Incremental overlap with the 2011 acceleration prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created an entire field of moiré quantum matter. The prediction was tested by clear clues from nature, which I value.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 theory prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group discovered the correlated and superconducting phases in 2018. This theory-plus-experiment split suits a three-person prize, but other groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Efetov, Yacoby) also made decisive contributions that I cannot rank.
assessment.maturity: The experimental findings have been reproduced widely and the field is large and active, but the interpretation of the superconductivity is still debated, so the maturity is moderate rather than complete.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unsettled.
Competing claims of priority among experimental groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recognition that cells organise their interior through liquid-liquid phase separation, with a statistical-physics description of these active droplets, brought physical concepts into cell biology and has had wide impact. It has an existential dimension in how we think about the organisation of life, though the question remains whether it is physics or biology.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated P granules as liquid droplets in 2009, and Jülicher provided the physical theory of active droplets. The configuration is coherent, but others (e.g. Rosen, Rosen-Brangwynne collaborators, Dill and earlier theorists) could be argued and I cannot verify the credit.
assessment.maturity: Impact is large but the biological generality and functional role of condensates are still disputed, so I regard it as somewhat early for a physics prize.
uncertainties: Debate about whether condensates are truly liquid-like and functionally relevant in vivo.
Whether the committee accepts biological physics of this kind within the physics prize remit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of radioactively powered kilonovae and the 2017 observation of AT2017gfo following GW170817 confirmed neutron-star mergers as a site of r-process nucleosynthesis, answering a question about the origin of heavy elements. It is a striking observational clue connecting nuclear physics and gravitation.
assessment.attribution: Metzger and collaborators made the foundational 2010 prediction and Kasen contributed radiative-transfer modelling; Foley led the discovery team of the optical counterpart (Swope). Many other groups (e.g. Coulter, Tanvir, Kilpatrick, Kasliwal) shared the observation, so the attribution is uncertain, and the underlying GW170817 detection was already recognised in 2017.
assessment.maturity: Only a single well-observed event so far, so independent confirmation is limited, though the interpretation is broadly accepted.
uncertainties: Only one clearly identified kilonova with a gravitational-wave counterpart.
Overlap with the 2017 prize for gravitational waves and unclear assignment between theory and observation.
